title: Distributional lower bound for Index
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\varepsilon$ be real, and let $c$ be a natural number. If every deterministic one-way protocol for the Index function on $n$-bit inputs with communication cost at most $c$ has error strictly greater than $\varepsilon$ under the uniform distribution on input pairs, then the public-coin one-way communication complexity of that function with error parameter $\varepsilon$ is strictly greater than $c$, as an extended natural number.
hypotheses_covered: Every deterministic one-way protocol for Index on $n$ bits of cost at most $c$ has uniform-distribution error greater than $\varepsilon$
replaced:
If every deterministic one-way protocol for $\mathrm{IND}_n$ of cost at most $c$ has
uniform-distributional error greater than $\varepsilon$, then the public-coin one-way
communication complexity of $\mathrm{IND}_n$ at error $\varepsilon$ is strictly greater than
$c$ (as an extended natural number).  This is the easy direction of Yao's minimax principle for
one-way protocols, applied to Index.
